desc.text: Southern Dry Cliff Open, lichen-dominated plant communities on dry, sunny south- to westfacing cliffs in rugged terrain, primarily in southeastern Minnesota. Vascular plants are sparse and restricted to crevices and ledges.

Southern Open Talus Open plant communities on steep talus slopes, usually below cliffs or bedrock outcrops in rugged terrain in southeastern Minnesota. Dominated by lichens or mosses, with sparse cover of trees or herbaceous plants.

Southern Algific Talus Cool, moist, open plant communities on steep northwest- to northeast-facing bluffs in karst landscapes of southeastern Minnesota. Characterized by cold, wet microclimate maintained by cold air and groundwater emanating from subterranean ice. Community supports northern plants uncommon in southern Minnesota and Pleistocene land snails.

Southern Wet Cflff Open moss-dominated plant communities on shaded northwest- to east-facing cliffs kept wet by seeping groundwater. Present in rugged terrain in southeastern Minnesota. Vascular plants are sparse, present mainly in crevices, on ledges, and on thick bryophyte mats.
Lake Superior Cliff Open plant communities on dry or, rarely, moist cliffs on the immediate shoreline of Lake Superior. Vascular plants are largely restricted to crevices and ledges.
Central Poor Dry Pine Woodland Ory jack pine woodlands on level, sandy /acustrine and outwash deposits in northcentral Minnesota. Crown fires and surface fires were common historically.

Central Rich Dry Pine Woodland Dry-mesic pine woodlands on sandy, level to gently undulating outwash deposits or occasionally on sandy inclusions in rolling to hummocky stagnation moraines and till plains. Crown fires and mild surface fires were common historically.

Central Dry-Mesic Pine-Hardwood Forest Dry-mesic pine, hardwood, or pine-hardwood forests on hummocky glacial moraines, often adjacent to outwash plains. Crown fires and mild surface fires were common historically.
Northern Dry-Sand Pine Woodland Dry jack pine or red pine woodlands on level to gently undulating, sandy outwash or lake plains. Crown and surface fires were common historically.

desc.text: Northern Poor Dry-Mesic Mixed Woodland Dry-mesic pine or black spruce woodlands, often mixed with paper birch and quaking aspen. Most common on relatively nutrient-poor, shallow, loamy soils over bedrock, but also present on sandy lacustrine plains. Crown and surface fires were common historically

desc.text: Northern Dry-Mesic Mixed Woodland Dry-mesic conifer, conifer-hardwood, or hardwood woodlands dominated by red pine, white pine, jack pine, black spruce, quaking aspen, or paper birch. Most common on sandy soils but also present on shallow, loamy soils over bedrock. Crown and surface fires were common historically.
Southern Dry-Mesic Pine-Oak Woodland Dry-mesic (or dry) hardwood or pine-hardwood woodlands on sand deposits, primarily in the bluff/ands of southeastern Minnesota.

Southern Dry-Mesic Oak-Aspen Forest Dry-mesic hardwood forests dominated by a mix of bur oak and quaking aspen. Present on hummocky stagnation moraines on well-drained, gravelly, loamy, calcareous till in northwestern Minnesota.

Southern Dry-Mesic Oak (Maple) Woodland Dry-mesic hardwood forests on undulatmg sand flats, hummocky moraines, and river bluffs. Present mostly on fine sand or sand-gravel soils. Often on south- or west-facing slopes but common also on flat to undulating sandy lake plains. Historically, fires were common in this community, and many stands are on sites occupied by brush/ands 100 years ago.
Southern Dry-Mesic Oak-Hickory Woodland Dry-mesic (or dry) deciduous woodlands on steep, exposed, south- to westfacing bluffs in southeastern Minnesota, often adjacent to bedrock bluff prairies.

Northwestern Mesic Aspen-Oak Woodland Mesic woodlands dominated by quaking aspen and bur oak with occasional jack pine. Present on level, sandy soils, occasionally capped with loamy sediment, on the Glacial Lake Agassiz plain. Moderate surface fires were common historically, and catastrophic fires occasional.

Northwestern Wet-Mesic Aspen Woodland Wet-mesic woodlands dominated by quaking aspen. Present on poorly drained, flat, sandy soils, occasionally capped with loamy sediment, on the Glacial Lake Agassiz plain and rarely on the Anoka Sand Plain. Surface fires were common historically, and catastrophic crown fires were occasional.

Northern Floristic Region . . l Northern Terrace Forest Wet-mesic deciduous forests on silty or sandy alluvium on level, occasionally flooded sites along medium and large rivers in the northern half of Minnesota.

desc.text: FORESTED RICH PEATLAND SYSTEM Northern Floristic Region Northern Rich Tamarack Swamp (Eastern Basin) Tamarack-dominated swamps on shallow to deep peat in basins and in depressions in abandoned river channels.

FORESTED RICH PEATLAND SYSTEM Northern F/oristic Region Northern Rich Tamarack Swamp (Water Track) Tamarack-dominated swamps on deep peat in large peat/and complexes on glacial Jake plains or large peat-filled basins. Typically occurs in settings influenced by lateral flow of mineral-rich groundwater, such as water tracks.
Southern Rich Conifer Swamp Tamarack-dominated swamps on shallow to deep peat in basins on moraines and outwash plains. Occasionally on floating mats at edges of ponds or lakes.

Inland Lake Sand/Gravel/Cobble Shore Plant communities characterized by variable cover of shrubs, forbs, graminoids, and aquatic plants on we/I-drained, wave-washed sand, gravel, or small cobbles on shores along inland lakes. Present in the zone between /ow-water level and the upper reach of storm waves or ice scouring.

Inland Lake Rocky Shore Sparsely vegetated plant communities on wave-washed bedrock, boulder, or large-cobble shores along inland lakes. Present in the zone between normal low-water level and the upper reach of storm waves or ice scouring.

Central Dry-Mesic Oak-Aspen Forest Dry-mesic hardwood or, rarely, hardwood-conifer forests, usually with northern red oak as a canopy dominant. Present on we/I-drained loamy or sandy soils, primarily on stagnation moraines and less frequently on till plains or glacial river terraces.

communities.name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Large-Flowered Trillium) Forest

desc.text: Central Mesic Hardwood Forest (Eastern) Mesic hardwood forests dominated by basswood, northern red oak, and sugar maple. Present on loamy or sandy loam soils on hummocky stagnation moraines and rolling till plains.
Central Mesic Hardwood Forest (Western) Mesic hardwood forests dominated most commonly by basswood and sugar maple. Present on well-drained loamy soils on rolling to hummocky stagnation moraines.

Central Mesic Cold-Slope Hardwood-Conifer Forest Hardwood-conifer forests on steep north-facing bluffs, often associated with algific talus slopes where cold air vents enhance the cool, moist microclimate of the community. Characterized by northern species otherwise absent in southeastern Minnesota.

communities.name: White Pine - Sugar Maple - Basswood Forest (Cold Slope)

desc.text: Central Wet-Mesic Hardwood Forest Wet-mesic hardwood and hardwood-conifer forests on somewhat poorly drained sandy loam soils on till plains and stream terraces. Soils are saturated for prolonged periods, either because of clayey subsoil horizons that impede drainage or because of high local water tables.

Northern Mesic Hardwood Forest Mesic to dry-mesic hardwood forests on well-drained to moderately welldrained loamy soils, most often on stagnation moraines and till plains and less frequently on bedrock hills.

communities.name: Red Oak - Sugar Maple - Basswood - (Bluebead Lily) Forest

desc.text: Northern Wet-Mesic Boreal Hardwood-Conifer Forest Wet-mesic or mesic hardwood and hardwood-conifer forests, most commonly on level, clayey sites with high local water tables on glacial Jake deposits, stagnation moraines, and till plains.

desc.text: Southern Dry-Mesic Oak Forest Dry-mesic hardwood forests occurring most often on thin, wind-deposited silt on crests and upper slopes of bedrock bluffs and less often on hummocky stagnation moraines in calcareous, partially sorted drift.

desc.text: MARSH SYSTEM Northern Floristic Region Northern Bu/rush-Spikerush Marsh Emergent marsh communities typically dominated by bulrushes or spike rush - es. Present along lakeshores and stream borders.
Lake Superior Coastal Marsh Emergent marshes in estuaries near river mouths along the shore of Lake Superior. Influenced by cyclic wind-driven changes in lake level. t

Sand/Gravel/Cobble River Shore Sparsely to densely vegetated plant communities on sand, gravel, or small cobbles on river shores. Characterized by annual herbaceous species, firmly rooted perennial species tolerant of inundation, and species dispersed by tubers and other floating propagules. Scoured annually during spring breakup and flooding by ice and currents, and following heavy rains.

Rocky River Shore Sparsely vegetated plant communities on bedrock or boulder substrates along river shores. Scoured annually during spring breakup by ice and strong currents and during other periods of flooding.

Clay/Mud River Shore Sparsely to densely vegetated plant communities on clay or silt substrates on river shorelines that flood in spring but are exposed as water levels recede over summer. RVx54 includes plant communities on slumping river embankments as well as river shorelines.

UPLAND PRAIRIE SYSTEM Northern Floristic Region [? Northern Mesic Savanna Sparsely treed and usually shrubby communities with grass-dominated ground layers on somewhat poorly drained to we/I-drained loam soils mainly formed in glacial till (sometimes water-reworked) and outwash deposits, and less frequently in lacustrine sediments. Present primarily on level to gently rolling sites. Drought stress is irregular in occurrence and usually not severe. Historically, these communities burned every few years.

Southern Floristic Region -z- - - - Southern Dry Savanna Sparsely treed communities with grass-dominated herbaceous ground layers on nearly level to steeply sloping sites with draughty soils. Moderate growing-season moisture deficits occur during most years, and severe moisture deficits are frequent, especially during periodic regional droughts. Trees are open grown, typically small and gnarled.

leads.text: Dry-mesic conifer-hardwood woodland or forest. Central Floristic (FDc) Region species present (Table FD-1, p.65). Canopy of jack pine, red pine, or white pine, or with evidence of pine in the past; most often mixed with quaking aspen, bur oak, and paper birch. Most frequent on flat sandy supraglacial drift, outwash, or lake sediments. On excessively drained to moderately well-drained sandy forest soils, generally lacking dark soil horizons deeper than 6in (15cm). Present in the MIM only rarely, in the Hardwood Hills Subsection from Becker County north and along the northern border of the Anoka Sand Plain Subsection.

Documented in the Hardwood Hills Subsection from Becker County north.

leads.text: Dry hardwood woodland, occasionally with some pine. Canopy of northern pin oak mixed with some northern red oak or red maple [almost never with red pine]. Most frequent on sandy lacustrine deposits. On excessively to somewhat excessively drained sandy forest soils, usually with some silty-clayey banding. Canopy of bur oak, usually mixed with other hardwood trees, especially quaking aspen, northern pin oak, and northern red oak [almost never with jack pine, white pine, or red pine]. Most frequent on rolling sandy supraglacial drift, outwash, or lake sediments. On somewhat excessively drained to well-drained forest soils with darkened surface horizons that indicate former cover of woodland or prairie. Present throughout the Hardwood Hills, Anoka Sand Plain, and St. Paul-Baldwin Plains & Moraines subsections.

Documented only in the Hardwood Hills Subsection from Becker County north to Polk County.

leads.text: Canopy strongly dominated by bur oak, northern pin oak, northern red oak, or white oak; occasionally with red maple or black cherry [almost never with basswood or American elm]. Most frequent on sandy lacustrine deposits and outwash. On excessively drained to well-drained sandy forest soils. Documented from Becker County southward through the Hardwood Hills, Anoka Sand Plain, and St. Paul-Baldwin Plains & Moraines subsections.

On well-drained or moderately well-drained forest soils, comparatively nutrient poor and often lacking dark surface horizons that would indicate former cover of prairie. Documented from northern Washington County to northern Wright County and then northwestward to Polk County.

Canopy a mix of basswood, black ash, quaking aspen, and paper birch [almost never with sugar maple, northern red oak, ironwood, big-toothed aspen, white pine, or red pine]. Canopy usually dominated by basswood, sugar maple, or northern red oak, with lesser amounts of paper birch; occasionally with quaking aspen, bur oak, or American elm [almost never with balsam fir or black ash]. Present on rolling to rugged supraglacial drift. Documented in the MIM from northern Washington County to northern Wright County and northwestward to Polk County.

leads.text: Dry-mesic hardwood forest, historically mixed with some pine and usually with shrubby understory. Canopy a mix of northern red oak, basswood, or paper birch; occasionally with bur oak, red maple, or white pine [almost never with American elm]. Most frequent on hummocky supraglacial drift and sandy outwash inclusions; occasionally on gravelly ice-contact features. On somewhat excessively drained forest soils often lacking subsoil horizons capable of perching rainfall or snowmelt.

leads.text: Mesic hardwood forest, rarely with conifers. Canopy dominated by basswood and sugar maple; often mixed with paper birch or northern red oak; sometimes with bur oak, quaking aspen, or American elm [almost never with white pine or red maple]. Most frequent on hummocky supraglacial drift; rarely on sandy outwash. On well-drained forest soils with subsoil horizons capable of perching rainfall and snowmelt, often with organic-rich surface horizons that suggest former occupation by woodland or prairie.

leads.text: Canopy a mix of basswood and northern red oak, with lesser amounts of sugar maple; occasionally with red maple, paper birch, big-toothed aspen, bur oak, and American elm. Most frequent on hummocky supraglacial drift; occasional on sandy outwash and sandy lake sediments. Generally limited to non-calcareous or somewhat calcareous drift of the Wadena, Rainy, and Superior lobes in central and eastern Minnesota. On excessively to moderately well-drained forest soils. Documented primarily south and east of Otter Tail County.

leads.text: Canopy a mix of basswood and sugar maple, with lesser amounts of paper birch; sometimes with quaking aspen, northern red oak, bur oak, and American elm [almost never with red maple or big-toothed aspen]. Most frequent on hummocky supraglacial drift; rarely on sandy outwash or sandy lake sediments. Generally limited to highly calcareous drift of the Red River and Des Moines lobes in western Minnesota. On well-drained forest soils with organic-rich surface horizons that suggest former occupation by woodland or prairie or on well-drained prairie soils Documented primarily in Otter Tail County and northward.

Canopy dominated by sugar maple, basswood, or northern red oak. Occasionally with red or American elm, ironwood, green ash, black ash, or bitternut hickory [almost never with paper birch or quaking aspen]. On somewhat excessively drained to somewhat poorly drained soils, comparatively nutrient rich and usually with dark surface horizons that indicate former cover of prairie. Documented from Douglas County southeastward to Iowa.

leads.text: Mesic hardwood forest. Canopy a mix of sugar maple, basswood, and northern red oak; sometimes with red elm, ironwood, American elm, and bitternut hickory [almost never with hackberry]. Most frequent on hummocky supraglacial drift; occasional on bedrock-controlled terrain. On well-drained to moderately well-drained forest soils lacking dark surface horizon or with thin dark surface horizon over light-colored horizon.

Most commonly on steep terrain, often where topography is controlled by underlying bedrock; occasional on coarse-loamy supraglacial drift. On coarse-loamy forest soils, often with darkened surface horizons that indicate former cover of prairie. Present on slopes of all aspects.

Spring ephemeral species often present in ground layer. Most frequent on supraglacial drift. Soils fine-loamy forest soils, occasionally with darkened surface horizons that indicate former cover of prairie. Most common on north- and east-facing slopes.

On somewhat excessively to well-drained, loamy forest soils, often lacking subsoil horizons that can perch water (or if present, these horizons are weakly developed).

leads.text: Wet-mesic hardwood forest. Canopy a mix of basswood and black ash, with lesser amounts of hackberry, box elder, and sugar maple. Most frequent on flat alluvium and channeled outwash along the Mississippi and Minnesota rivers and their tributaries; occasional on flat supraglacial drift or till plains. On moderately well-drained to poorly drained forest soils with darkened surface horizons.

Canopy of silver maple, black ash, basswood, bur oak, or green ash; occasionally with American elm [almost never has hackberry or cottonwood]. Rare, documented only along the border of the MIM with the southwestern part of the MDL.

leads.text: Wet riparian hardwood forest. Canopy of basswood, black ash, bur oak, silver maple, or green ash. Shrub-layer cover typically >25%. Cover of ferns and fern allies relatively high (>25%), usually with two or more species present. Most often on rarely flooded stream or river terrace; evidence of recent flooding generally lacking.

leads.text: Very wet riparian hardwood forest. Canopy strongly dominated by silver maple with scattered individuals of other tree species [almost never has bur oak]. Shrub layer usually absent or with <25% cover. Cover of ferns and fern allies relatively low (often <5%), usually with only one species present. Dense cover of ostrich fern may be present in swales. Most often on annually flooded river floodplain; ice-scars, piles of woody debris, active levees, and meander scrolls typically present.

leads.text: Wet or very wet riparian hardwood forest. Southern Floristic (FFs) Region species present (Table FF-2, p. 164). Canopy of silver maple, green ash, box elder, or American elm; occasionally with hackberry and cottonwood [almost never has bur oak].

leads.text: Wet riparian hardwood forest. Canopy a mix of American elm, silver maple, and box elder; sometimes with hackberry, basswood, black ash, or green ash. Comparatively low cover (typically <25%) of grasses and sedges. Most frequent on alluvial cut terraces that flood occasionally for short periods. On moderately well-drained to somewhat poorly drained silty forest soils.

leads.text: Very wet riparian hardwood forest. Canopy strongly dominated by silver maple with lesser amounts of green ash; sometimes with cottonwood [almost never has basswood or black ash]. Comparatively high cover (typically >25%) of grasses and sedges. Most frequent on annually flooded alluvial terraces. On poorly drained silty or sandy forest soils subject to scour and deposition.

Canopy dominated by black ash or white cedar, mixed with tamarack, paper birch, and yellow birch; occasionally with American elm and red maple. Most frequent in lowland areas on deep glacial drift away from major rivers; groundwater seepage may or may not be evident.

leads.text: Wet hardwood forest, occasionally with scattered conifers. Canopy dominated by black ash with lesser amounts of paper birch, American elm, yellow birch, red maple, and tamarack.

leads.text: Wet hardwood forest, occasionally with scattered conifers. Canopy dominated by black ash, sometimes mixed with lesser amounts of paper birch, basswood, white pine, and red maple. On somewhat poorly drained to poorly drained mineral soils with mucky surface.
leads.rt: If c + c' < 0 ....WFn55 Northern Wet Ash Swamp p. 191

leads.text: Very wet hardwood forest, occasionally with scattered conifers. Canopy dominated by black ash mixed with lesser amounts of yellow birch, paper birch, and red maple; occasionally with tamarack [rarely or never with basswood or white pine]. On very poorly drained, shallow organic soils.
leads.rt: If c + c' ≥ 0 ....WFn64 Northern Very Wet Ash Swamp p. 195

leads.text: Wet hardwood forest, lacking conifers. Southern Floristic (WFs) Region species present (Table WF-2, p. 184). Canopy dominated by black ash, occasionally mixed with basswood, sugar maple, American elm, or green ash; or canopy dominated by quaking aspen, sometimes with black ash or bur oak [almost never has red maple, tamarack, or white cedar]. Commonly at base of valley wall or bluff along river or stream, with springs or broad groundwater seepage zones usually evident; or on level to gently rolling outwash plain.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 go to d

leads.text: Canopy strongly dominated by black ash, often with other hardwood species, especially basswood, sugar maple, and American elm. Most common on alluvium or colluvium at base of valley wall or bluff along St. Croix, Mississippi, Minnesota, or Cannon River, or smaller tributary. Springs or broad groundwater seepage zones usually evident; water noticeably cold.
leads.rt: If d + d' < 0 ....WFs57 Southern Wet Ash Swamp p. 201

leads.text: Canopy dominated by quaking aspen, sometimes with black ash or bur oak. Most common on sandy loam on level to gently rolling outwash plain, typically on slightly raised mineral island in large open wet meadow or in transition zone between wet meadow and forested upland. Springs and seepage zones absent.
leads.rt: If d + d' ≥ 0 ....WFs55 Southern Wet Aspen Forest p. 199

leads.text: Conifer swamp with canopy dominated by tamarack, sometimes with black spruce. Northern Floristic (FPn) Region species are present (Table FP-1, page 208). In the MIM, documented only in Hardwood Hills Subsection.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 ....FPn82 Northern Rich Tamarack Swamp (Western Basin) p.214

leads.text: Conifer swamp with canopy dominated by tamarack with occasional paper birch or other hardwoods. Southern Floristic (FPs) Region species present (Table FP-2, page 209). Documented throughout the MIM.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 ....FPs63 Southern Rich Conifer Swamp p.218

leads.text: Wooded peatland; trees taller than 15ft (5m) have >25% cover. Sites burned in the past may lack tree canopy but shade-tolerant understory species persist for decades.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 ....APn81 Northern Poor Conifer Swamp p.225

leads.text: Open to sparsely wooded peatland; trees taller than 15ft (5m) usually have <25% cover.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 ....APn91 Northern Poor Fen p. 230

leads.text: Open, lichen-dominated community on talus substrate composed of boulders and rock fragments eroded from upslope cliff or rock outcrop. Generally present on steep slope below cliff.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 ....CTs23 Southern Open Talus p. 240

leads.text: Open, lichen, moss, or herbaceous plant community on substrate composed of vertical or nearly vertical bedrock exposure (cliff) generally greater than 6ft (2m) tall.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 go to b

leads.text: Dry cliff, generally with south to west aspect and majority of cliff face exposed to direct sunlight. Typically present on upper slope of steep river bluff. Vascular plants sparse, but commonly including species characteristic of Dry Bedrock Bluff Prairies (UPs13c). Mosses and algae sparse. Crustose lichens dense.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≤ 0 ....CTs12 Southern Dry Cliff p. 237

leads.text: Dry-mesic to wet cliff, generally with northwest to east aspect and majority of cliff face shaded. Vascular plants sparse to dense; species characteristic of Mesic Hardwood Forest communities commonly present. Mosses, lichens, and algae have moderate to dense cover.
leads.rt: If b + b' > 0 go to c

leads.text: Dry-mesic to mesic cliff with obvious groundwater seepage either absent or present on <1/3 of cliff face. Vascular plants common, although largely restricted to crevices and ledges. Mosses and lichens common, with lichens generally having greater cover. Algae common.
leads.rt: If c + c' ≤ 0 ....CTs33 Southern Mesic Cliff p. 242

leads.text: Wet cliff with groundwater seepage emerging through crevices, especially along contacts between different bedrock layers; seepage typically covers >1/3 of cliff face. Usually present on lower slope of steep bluff. Vascular plants often dense; present on ledges, in crevices, and on thick bryophyte mats that cover cliff face. Mosses more abundant than lichens. Algae common. Community is rare in the MIM.
leads.rt: If c + c' > 0 ....CTs53 Southern Wet Cliff p. 250

leads.text: Species-rich to somewhat species-poor grassland or savanna dominated by a combination of tall and midheight grass species, including big bluestem (Andropogon gerardii), little bluestem (Schizachyrium scoparium), prairie dropseed (Sporobolus heterolepis), side-oats grama, and porcupine grass. Present on landforms where substrate and topography sharply limit moisture availability. Soils are somewhat excessively to excessively drained sands and loamy sands, sometimes with a substantial gravel fraction, and loams, often sandy with much gravel, on steep slopes in glacial drift. Dark-colored surface layer is generally thin and may be poorly developed or absent in dune sands.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 go to b

leads.text: Trees >6ft (2m) tall (bur oak, northern pin oak) rare or absent (cover <10%); woody plants mostly leadplant (Amorpha canescens), smooth sumac (Rhus glabra), and prairie rose (Rosa arkansana). Eastern red cedar sometimes present as a result of fire-suppression.
leads.rt: UPs13 Southern Dry Prairie p. 284

leads.text: Trees >6ft (2m) tall (bur oak, northern pin oak) present as scattered individuals or in scattered small clumps (total cover >10%). Shrubs (including oak "grubs" up to 6ft tall) usually common (cover 10-70%). Frequent shrub species include American hazelnut (Corylus americana), chokecherry (Prunus virginiana), and juneberries (Amelanchier spp.), in addition to species listed above for UPs13.
leads.rt: UPs14 Southern Dry Savanna p. 289

leads.text: Species-rich grassland or savanna dominated by tallgrass species, invariably including some combination of big bluestem, Indian grass (Sorghastrum nutans), and prairie dropseed; Wetland Prairie species (e.g., prairie cordgrass [Spartina pectinata], tall meadow-rue [Thalictrum dasycarpum]) often present, but less abundant. On deep, loamy, moderately well-drained and well-drained soils with thick, dark-colored surface horizon.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 go to c

leads.text: Trees >6ft (2m) tall rare or absent (cover <10%). Shrubs mostly leadplant and prairie rose; American hazelnut and gray dogwood often present. Quaking aspen and eastern red cedar trees sometimes present as a result of fire suppression; aspen "suckers" frequently present.
leads.rt: UPs23 Southern Mesic Prairie p. 294

leads.text: Trees >6ft (2m) tall (principally bur oak) present as scattered individuals or in scattered small clumps (total cover >10%). Shrubs (may include oak "grubs" up to 6ft tall) usually common (cover 10-70%); chokecherry and smooth sumac are most common, along with shrubs listed above for UPs23.
leads.rt: UPs24 Southern Mesic Savanna p. 298

leads.text: Open, graminoid- or shrub-dominated peatland. Northern Floristic (OPn) Region species, such as ericaceous shrubs, typically present (Table OP-1, p. 303).
leads.rt: If a + a' ≤ 0 go to b

leads.text: In small basin, along peatland edge (lagg), or on floating mat adjacent to lake or pond. Water track features not apparent on aerial photos.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≤ 0 go to c

leads.text: Shrubby peatland dominated by leatherleaf, bog birch (Betula pumila), or sweet gale (Myrica gale); graminoids dominated by broad-leaved sedges and grasses (e.g., bluejoint, lake sedge [Carex lacustris]). Often associated with peatland bordering lake or river shore or in lagg between peatland and upland. Periodically exposed to surface flooding.
leads.rt: If c + c' < 0 ....OPn81 Northern Shrub Shore Fen p. 305

leads.text: Graminoid or shrubby peatland; shrubs, if present, typically dominated by willows; graminoids dominated by fine-leaved species (e.g., fen wiregrass sedge, creeping sedge). Present in basin or on floating mat adjacent to lake or river. Not subject to surface flooding.
leads.rt: If c + c' ≥ 0 ....OPn92 Northern Rich Fen (Basin) p. 312

leads.text: In large plain or in smaller linear-shaped peatland. Water tracks that follow gradual slope of peatland are often evident on aerial photos.
leads.rt: If b + b' > 0 go to d

leads.text: Graminoid or shrubby peatland in broad water track. Seepage areas and marl absent. Ribbed pattern of alternating shrub-dominated peat ridges may be present.
leads.rt: If d + d' ≤ 0 ....OPn91 Northern Rich Fen (Water Track) p. 308

leads.text: Graminoid peatland in narrow channels dissecting swamp forest. Seepage discharge areas present, often with marl precipitate. The moss Scorpidium scorpoides is usually present.
leads.rt: If d + d' > 0 ....OPn93 Northern Extremely Rich Fen p. 315

leads.text: Open, graminoid-dominated peatland. Prairie Floristic (OPp) Region species present (Table OP-2, p. 304).

sp.s: Helianthus giganteus, H. grosseserratus, or H. nuttallii

leads.rt: If a + a' > 0 go to e

leads.text: Dominated by fen wiregrass sedge (Carex lasiocarpa). Wetland Prairie species uncommon. Pools with marl or tufa deposits absent. Usually in shallow depression or drainageway.
leads.rt: If e + e' ≤ 0 ....OPp91 Prairie Rich Fen p. 318

leads.text: Areas dominated by sterile sedge or hair-like beak rush almost always present. Wetland Prairie species (including big bluestem [Andropogon gerardii], mat muhly grass [Muhlenbergia richardsonis], Riddell's goldenrod [Solidago riddellii], prairie loosestrife, and other species) are usually present. Pools with marl or tufa deposits typically present. On slight slope; not in depression.
leads.rt: If e + e' > 0 ....OPp93 Prairie Extremely Rich Fen p. 323
FPn73 Northern Rich Alder Swamp p. 210

leads.text: Open, graminoid- or shrub-dominated wetland. Northern Floristic (WMn) Region species present (Table WM-1, p. 330). Dominant graminoid typically lake sedge, tussock sedge (Carex stricta), beaked sedge, or bluejoint (Calamagrostis canadensis).
leads.rt: If a + a' ≤ 0 ....WMn82 Northern Wet Meadow/Carr p. 332

leads.text: Open, graminoid-, shrub-, or forb-dominated wetland. Southern Floristic (WMs) Region species present (Table WM-2, p. 331). Dominant graminoid typically tussock sedge (Carex stricta), aquatic sedge (C. aquatilis), prairie sedge (C. prairea), hairy-fruited sedge (C. trichocarpa), slough sedge (C. atherodes), or whitetop (Scolochloa festucacea).
leads.rt: If a + a' > 0 go to b

leads.text: Dominated by graminoids or shrubs (or occasionally by touch-me-not [Impatiens spp.] in meadows associated with seepage openings in hardwood swamps). Dominant graminoid typically tussock sedge (Carex stricta), aquatic sedge (C. aquatilis), prairie sedge (C. prairea), or hairy-fruited sedge (C. trichocarpa). Usually associated with groundwater seepage area at base of river terrace or beach ridge, or on gentle slope. Can also occur in level wetland dissected by stream or river.
leads.rt: If b + b' < 0 ....WMs83 Southern Seepage Meadow/Carr p. 335

leads.text: Dominated by graminoids, typically slough sedge or whitetop (Scolochloa festucacea). Usually present in shallow wetland basin (prairie pothole); occasionally present along shore of lake or river. Uncommon in the MIM.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≥ 0 ....WMs92 Southern Basin Wet Meadow/Carr p. 340

leads.text: Emergent marsh dominated by cattails, usually with >50% cover. Sedges (Carex spp.) commonly present. Substrate is mineral soil or peat, often forming floating mat. Associated with sheltered to moderately wave-washed shore or isolated basin.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≤ 0 ....MRn83 Northern Mixed Cattail Marsh p. 346

leads.text: Emergent marsh dominated by bulrushes or spikerushes (e.g., soft stem bulrush [Scirpus validus], river bulrush [S. fluviatilis], hardstem bulrush [S. acutus], slender bulrush [S. heterochaetus], Small's spikerush [Eleocharis smallii]). Substrate is mineral soil. Associated with wave-washed shore or stream margin.
leads.rt: If a + a' > 0 ....MRn93 Northern Bulrush-Spikerush Marsh p. 349
WPs54 Southern Wet Prairie p. 356

leads.text: Dry-mesic mixed hardwood-pine forest. Canopy dominated by black oak and white pine, sometimes with white oak, paper birch, northern pin oak, northern red oak, quaking aspen, or bitternut hickory [almost never with shagbark hickory or black cherry]. Limited to excessively drained sandy forest soils, usually lacking darkened surface horizons that indicate former cover of woodland or prairie. Community is uncommon.
leads.rt: if a + a' < 0....FDs27 Southern Dry-Mesic Pine-Oak Woodland p. 81

leads.text: Dry-mesic hardwood forest. Canopy a mix of bur oak, shagbark hickory, and northern pin oak with lesser amounts of American elm; sometimes with black cherry, black walnut, and northern red oak [almost never with white pine or black oak]. On somewhat excessively to well-drained silty forest soils, commonly with darkened surface horizons that indicate former cover of woodland or prairie.
leads.rt: if a + a' ≥ 0....FDs38 Southern Dry-Mesic Oak-Hickory Woodland p. 94

leads.text: Mesic mixed hardwood-conifer forest, usually with high conifer cover (typically > 25%). Central Floristic (MHc) Region species present (Table MH-2, p.103). Canopy a mix of sugar maple and northern red oak with lesser amounts of basswood, white pine, and ironwood; often with balsam fir, yellow birch, paper birch, and white oak [almost never with American elm or slippery elm]. Documented only in cool, shaded, moist microhabitats on north- and northeast-facing slopes in deep valleys. On very rocky colluvium, often with cold-air (algific) vents.
leads.rt: if a + a' < -2....MHc38 Central Mesic Cold-Slope Hardwood-Conifer Forest p. 132

leads.text: Mesic or wet-mesic hardwood forest, rarely with conifers or if present, conifer cover is usually <25%. Southern Floristic (MHs) Region species present (Table MH-3, p.104). Canopy usually dominated by sugar maple, basswood, northern red oak, or a combination of these species, sometimes with white oak, ironwood, American elm, or red elm [almost never with balsam fir or yellow birch]. On relatively deep, well-developed soils.
leads.rt: if a + a' ≥ -2 go to b

leads.text: Mesic hardwood forest. Canopy a mix of northern red oak, sugar maple, and basswood with lesser amounts of white oak and ironwood; sometimes with American elm or bitternut hickory [almost never with rock elm]. Most often on well-drained, silty forest or relict prairie soils formed in loess over bedrock.

leads.text: Canopy a mix of northern red oak and white oak with lesser amounts of basswood; sometimes with American elm, sugar maple, shagbark hickory, bur oak, red elm, black cherry, ironwood, northern pin oak, or hackberry.

leads.text: Canopy a mix of sugar maple, basswood, and northern red oak with lesser amounts of white oak and ironwood; sometimes with bitternut hickory and American elm [almost never with shagbark hickory, hackberry, or northern pin oak].
leads.rt: if c + c' > 0 go to d

leads.text: Mesic hardwood forest, occasionally with conifers. Canopy a mix of northern red oak and basswood with lesser amounts of sugar maple, white oak, and ironwood; occasionally with paper birch, white pine, American elm, or bitternut hickory. Spring ephemeral species often present in ground layer, although less abundant and diverse than in MHs39. Most often on relict prairie soils with dark surface horizons; occasionally on forest soils.
leads.rt: if d + d' ≤ 0....MHs38 Southern Mesic Oak-Basswood Forest p. 142

leads.text: Mesic hardwood forest, very rarely with conifers. Canopy a mix of basswood and sugar maple with lesser amounts of northern red oak, ironwood, and American elm; sometimes with bitternut hickory, black ash, or red elm [almost never with paper birch or white pine although white pine may be present in stands on upper slopes adjacent to white pine-covered ridges]. Spring ephemeral species such as Dutchman's breeches (Dicentra cucullaria), cut-leaved toothwort (Cardamine concatenata), and white trout lily (Erythronium albidum) typically abundant in ground layer from mid-April through May. Most often on forest soils with thin dark horizon over light-colored horizon; occasionally on relict prairie soils.

leads.text: Wet-mesic hardwood forest. Canopy a mix of sugar maple, basswood, black ash, and American elm with lesser amounts of hackberry; sometimes with red elm, bur oak, box elder, blue beech, or rock elm [almost never with white oak]. Most often on alluvial deposit on bottomland in dissected bedrock terrain. On moderately well-drained soils, usually formed in silt, but sometimes formed in stratified sand or gravel.
leads.rt: if b + b' > 0....MHs49 Southern Wet-Mesic Hardwood Forest p. 151

leads.text: Wet riparian hardwood forest in valley of tributary to Mississippi River or occasionally in Mississippi River valley. Canopy a mix of several species including American elm, green ash, cottonwood, basswood, hackberry, red elm, black ash, black walnut, and box elder; occasionally with silver maple or swamp white oak. Most often on alluvial terrace or stream bottom that floods occasionally for short periods. On moderately well-drained to poorly drained silty forest soils.
leads.rt: if a + a' < 0....FFs59 Southern Terrace Forest p. 172

leads.text: Very wet riparian hardwood forest in Mississippi River valley. Canopy strongly dominated by silver maple, sometimes mixed with minor amounts of green ash, American elm, cottonwood, and hackberry [almost never with box elder or basswood]. Most often on alluvial terrace that floods annually for long periods. On poorly drained sandy forest soils subject to scour and deposition.
leads.rt: if a + a' ≥ 0....FFs68 Southern Floodplain Forest p. 177

leads.text: Talus wet-mesic to wet with considerable silty, organic soil development. Cold air vents and cold ground water seepage zones present; setting characterized by cold, moist microclimate that is maintained well into growing season. Aspect is generally north (to east). Vascular plants often dense, with northern species, wetland species, and rare species often present. Moss cover dense, forming thick mats, with northern species common. Often associated with Central Cold-Slope Mesic Hardwood Forest (MHc38). Community is rare.

Aspect primarily north. Vascular plants often include northern species and rare species. Mosses often form thick mats, with lichens and algae common; northern bryophyte species usually present. Community is rare, usually occurring within larger area of Southern Mesic Cliff (CTs33).

leads.text: Wet cliff, usually present on lower part of steep bluff, with groundwater seepage emerging through crevices, especially along contacts between bedrock layers. Vascular plants often dense, occurring on ledges, in crevices, and on thick bryophyte mats that cover cliff face; rare species often present. Mosses more abundant than lichens. Algae common. Community is rare.

On deep, loamy, moderately well-drained and well-drained soils with thick, dark-colored surface horizon.

leads.text: Trees >6ft (2m) tall rare or absent (cover <10%). Shrubs mostly leadplant and prairie rose; American hazelnut and gray dogwood (Cornus racemosa) often present. Quaking aspen and eastern red cedar trees sometimes present as a result of fire suppression; aspen "suckers" frequently present.
leads.rt: UPs23 Southern Mesic Prairie p. 294

leads.text: Trees >6ft (2m) tall (principally bur oak) present as scattered individuals or in scattered clumps. Shrubs (may include oak "grubs" up to 6ft tall) usually common (cover 10-70%); chokecherry and smooth sumac are most common, along with shrub species listed above for UPs23.
leads.rt: UPs24 Southern Mesic Savanna p. 298
OPp93 Prairie Extremely Rich Fen p. 323

leads.text: Open, graminoid- or shrub-dominated wetland. Northern Floristic (WMn) Region species present (Table WM-1, p. 330). Dominant graminoid typically lake sedge (Carex lacustris) or beaked sedge (C. utriculata). Standing water present; community often near marsh or open water.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≤ 0 ....WMn82 Northern Wet Meadow/Carr p. 332

leads.text: Open, graminoid-, shrub-, or forb-dominated wetland. Southern Floristic (WMs) Region species present (Table WM-2, p. 331). Dominant graminoid typically tussock sedge (Carex stricta), hairy-fruited sedge (Carex trichocarpa), aquatic sedge (Carex aquatilis), or prairie sedge (Carex prairea). Touch-me-not (Impatiens spp.) abundant and often dominant in meadows associated with seepage openings in hardwood swamps. Community present in groundwater seepage area at base of river terrace or slope in dissected terrain.
leads.rt: If a + a' > 0 ....WMs83 Southern Seepage Meadow/Carr p. 335

leads.text: Emergent marsh dominated by cattails (Typha spp.), usually with >50% cover. Sedges (Carex spp.) commonly present. Substrate is mineral soil or peat, often forming floating mat. Associated with sheltered to moderately wave-washed shore.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≤ 0 ....MRn83 Northern Mixed Cattail Marsh p. 346

leads.text: Emergent marsh dominated by bulrushes or spikerushes (e.g., soft stem bulrush [Scirpus validus], river bulrush [Scirpus fluviatilis], hardstem bulrush [Scirpus acutus], slender bulrush [Scirpus heterochaetus], or Small's spikerush [Eleocharis smallii]). Substrate is mineral soil. Associated with wave-washed shore.
leads.rt: If a + a' > 0 ....MRn93 Northern Bulrush-Spikerush Marsh p. 349
WPs54 Southern Wet Prairie p. 356

leads.text: Dry pine or oak woodland. [Canopy almost never has black spruce, red maple, big-toothed aspen, northern red oak, or heart-leaved birch.] Usually on excessively drained or somewhat excessively drained, deep, coarse sands or very thin soils over bedrock.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 go to b

leads.text: Trees of normal height and form. Canopy dominated by jack or red pine [almost never has northern pin oak]. Present on flat, sandy landform with deep soils. Rare, but known to occur along the western border of NSU.
leads.rt: If b + b' < 0 ....FDn12 Northern Dry-Sand Pine Woodland p. 103

leads.text: Trees often stunted or with poor form. Canopy dominated by jack pine, red pine, white pine, or northern pin oak. Present on scoured bedrock outcrop with thin soils. Common across the Border Lakes Subsection.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≥ 0 ....FDn22 Northern Dry-Bedrock Pine (Oak) Woodland p. 106

leads.text: Dry-mesic or mesic woodland or forest. Canopy is variable. Usually on coarse-loamy moraine or on till over bedrock.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 go to c

leads.text: Dry-mesic woodland. Canopy often dominated by quaking aspen, paper birch, or red pine [almost never has black spruce or white cedar]. Usually in area of deep glacial drift, especially along the western edge of NSU.
leads.rt: If c + c' < 0 ....FDn33 Northern Dry-Mesic Mixed Woodland p. 112

leads.text: Dry-mesic forest or mesic woodland. Canopy often dominated by quaking aspen, paper birch, black spruce, or jack pine [almost never has northern red oak]. Occurs on scoured bedrock terrain throughout NSU.
leads.rt: If c + c' ≥ 0 go to d

leads.text: Poor, dry-mesic conifer woodland, sometimes mixed with hardwoods. Canopy often dominated by jack pine, black spruce, red pine, or white pine [almost never has white cedar or heart-leaved birch]. Typically on upper slope or ridge.
leads.rt: If d + d' ≤ 0 ....FDn32 Northern Poor Dry-Mesic Mixed Woodland p. 109

leads.text: Mesic hardwood-conifer or conifer forest. Canopy often dominated by white pine, red pine, quaking aspen, paper birch, or white cedar. Old pine or cedar stumps often present in stands dominated by aspen or birch. Typically on lower slope or flat.
leads.rt: If d + d' > 0 ....FDn43 Northern Mesic Mixed Forest p. 115

leads.text: Mesic hardwood, hardwood-conifer, or conifer forest. Sugar maple, basswood, northern red oak, white cedar, or yellow birch important in canopy [almost never has balsam poplar, bur oak, or big-toothed aspen]. Most commonly on scoured bedrock terrain; occasionally on moraine or till plain; not documented on lake plain. On well-drained to moderately well-drained coarse-loamy soils.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≤ 0 go to b

leads.text: Mesic hardwood forest, occasionally with some conifers. Canopy often dominated by sugar maple, basswood, or northern red oak [almost never has white spruce, white cedar, or heart-leaved birch]. Present on scoured bedrock terrain in the North Shore Highlands Subsection in St. Louis and Lake Counties or on moraine or till plain elsewhere in NSU.
leads.rt: If b + b' < 0 go to c

leads.text: Mesic hardwood forest. Canopy dominated by sugar maple, northern red oak, or basswood canopy [almost never has black ash].
leads.rt: If c + c' < 0 ....MHn35 Northern Mesic Hardwood Forest p. 136

leads.text: Rich mesic hardwood forest. Canopy dominated by sugar maple with lesser amounts of basswood [almost never has red maple, quaking aspen, or ironwood].
leads.rt: If c + c' ≥ 0 ....MHn47 Northern Rich Mesic Hardwood Forest p. 147

leads.text: Mesic or wet-mesic hardwood, conifer, or hardwood-conifer forest. Canopy often dominated by sugar maple, paper birch, yellow birch, or white cedar [almost never has northern red oak or ironwood]. Usually on steep, scoured bedrock terrain in the North Shore Highlands Subsection in Lake and Cook Counties; present rarely on bedrock highs elsewhere in NSU.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≥ 0 ....MHn45 Northern Mesic Hardwood (Cedar) Forest p. 142

leads.text: Wet-mesic hardwood or hardwood-conifer forest. Quaking aspen, paper birch, balsam poplar, black ash, or basswood important in canopy [almost never has northern red oak]. Present on till plain, scoured bedrock terrain, moraine, or lake plain. On moderately well-drained to somewhat poorly drained fine-loamy soils.
leads.rt: If a + a' > 0 go to d

leads.text: Wet-mesic hardwood forest, commonly mixed with conifers (or has evidence of conifer dominance in the past). Canopy most often dominated by quaking aspen, paper birch, or balsam poplar [almost never has yellow birch].
leads.rt: If d + d' < 0 ....MHn44 Northern Wet-Mesic Boreal Hardwood-Conifer Forest p. 139

leads.text: Wet-mesic hardwood forest, rarely mixed with conifers. Canopy dominated by black ash or with variable mixture of black ash, basswood, quaking aspen, bur oak, or red maple [almost never has balsam fir or big-toothed aspen].
leads.rt: If d + d' ≥ 0 ....MHn46 Northern Wet-Mesic Hardwood Forest p. 144

leads.text: Wet riparian hardwood forest. Canopy dominated by silver maple or black ash; typically with green ash, basswood, bur oak, or American elm. Usually on alluvial or cut terrace that floods rarely or occasionally. On moderately well-drained to poorly drained silty or, less often, sandy soils.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 ....FFn57 Northern Terrace Forest p. 164

leads.text: Very wet riparian hardwood forest. Canopy dominated by silver maple, with green ash, black ash, or American elm [almost never has bur oak or basswood]. Usually on annually flooded alluvial plain along medium or large river. Windrowed debris, ice scars on tree bases, freshly deposited silt and sand, or other evidence of recent flooding typical. On poorly drained sandy soils. Rare in NSU.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 ....FFn67 Northern Floodplain Forest p. 166

leads.text: Wet-mesic or wet conifer forest, usually with some hardwoods. Canopy dominated by white cedar, sometimes with abundant black ash. Feathermosses often important in the ground layer.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 ....WFn53 Northern Wet Cedar Forest p. 177

leads.text: Wet or very wet hardwood forest, often with some conifers. Canopy dominated by black ash with quaking aspen, white spruce, and white cedar [almost never has black spruce]. Ground layer characterized by sparse cover of Plagiomnium (dark-green, thin-leaved mosses).
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 go to b

leads.text: Wet hardwood forest, usually with scattered conifers. Canopy typically closed, with crowns touching or overlapping. Dominated by black ash with quaking aspen or balsam poplar. Ground layer hummocky, with upland forest herbs common on hummocks and around tree bases and wet forest species in mucky hollows.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≤ 0 ....WFn55 Northern Wet Ash Swamp p. 180

leads.text: Very wet hardwood forest, usually with scattered conifers. Canopy interrupted, with crowns not touching. Dominated by black ash, sometimes with white cedar or white spruce [almost never has quaking aspen, balsam poplar, American elm, or green ash]. Grasses and sedges often important in ground layer.
leads.rt: If b + b' > 0 ....WFn64 Northern Very Wet Ash Swamp p. 183

leads.text: Conifer swamp with canopy dominated by white cedar, black spruce, or a mixture of the two species (rarely by tamarack); OR shrub swamp dominated by speckled alder or other tall shrubs. Present in basin peatland or in wetland adjacent to river.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≤ 0 go to b

leads.text: Conifer swamp, tree cover >25%. White cedar, balsam fir, black spruce, or tamarack important in canopy. Speckled alder frequent in shrub layer but generally with <25% cover.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≤ 0 go to c

leads.text: Canopy dominated by black spruce.
leads.rt: If c + c' < 0 ....FPn62 Northern Rich Spruce Swamp (Basin) p. 196

leads.text: Canopy strongly dominated by white cedar with occasional balsam fir, black spruce, or tamarack.
leads.rt: If c + c' ≥ 0 ....FPn63 Northern Cedar Swamp p. 198

leads.text: Shrub swamp; shrub cover >50% and tree cover <25%. Usually dominated by speckled alder.
leads.rt: If b + b' > 0 ....FPn73 Northern Alder Swamp p. 205

leads.text: Conifer swamp with canopy dominated by black spruce, tamarack, or a mixture of the two species. Present in basin or in large peatland on glacial lake plain.
leads.rt: If a + a' > 0 go to d

leads.text: Typically present in interior of large peatland on glacial lake plain. Often associated with rich fen water track.
leads.rt: If d + d' < 0 go to e

leads.text: Canopy typically dominated by black spruce, usually mixed with tamarack.
leads.rt: If e + e' < 0 ....FPn71 Northern Rich Spruce Swamp (Water Track) p. 201

leads.text: Canopy typically dominated by tamarack, occasionally mixed with black spruce. Often borders rich fen water track; can form teardrop-shaped island.
leads.rt: If e + e' ≥ 0 ....FPn81 Northern Rich Tamarack Swamp (Water Track) p. 207

leads.text: Present in peatland basin or at edge of large peatland.
leads.rt: If d + d' ≥ 0 ....FPn82 Northern Rich Tamarack Swamp (Western Basin) p. 209

leads.text: Wooded peatland; trees taller than 16ft (5m) have >25% cover. If burned in past, may lack tree canopy but shade-tolerant understory species persist for decades.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 go to b

leads.text: Only bog species are present (see Appendix D). Minerotrophic species, if present, are restricted to tree seedlings and are short lived.
leads.rt: If b + b' = 0 ....APn80 Northern Spruce Bog p. 219

leads.text: Both minerotrophic and bog species are present.
leads.rt: If b + b' > 0 ....APn81 Northern Poor Conifer Swamp p. 222

leads.text: Open to sparsely wooded peatland; trees taller than 16ft (5m) usually have <25% cover.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 go to c

leads.text: Only bog species are present (see Appendix D).
leads.rt: If c + c' = 0 ....APn90 Northern Open Bog p. 225

leads.text: Both minerotrophic and bog species are present.
leads.rt: If c + c' > 0 ....APn91 Northern Poor Fen p. 228

leads.text: Substrate composed of boulders and rock fragments (talus) eroded from upslope cliff or rock outcrop. Present on steep slope below cliff.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 go to b

leads.text: Open community with little or no shrub or tree cover. Lichens are predominant cover, with foliose species common. Talus fragments 12-36in (30-90cm) in diameter. Habitat generally dry at surface but often moist below talus. Frequently occurs below zone of shrub-dominated talus (i.e., Northern Scrub Talus).
leads.rt: If b + b' ≤ 0 ....CTn12 Northern Open Talus p. 236

leads.text: Shrub-dominated community, often with scattered small, open-grown trees. Woody plants are dominant cover (generally >25%). Talus fragments <12in (30cm) in diameter. Habitat varies from dry to mesic. Frequently occurs above zone of open, lichen-dominated talus (i.e., Northern Open Talus).
leads.rt: If b + b' > 0 ....CTn24 Northern Scrub Talus p. 238

leads.text: Substrate composed of vertical or nearly vertical bedrock exposure (cliff), generally greater than 6ft (2m) tall.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 go to c

leads.text: Cliff present on immediate shoreline of Lake Superior where “lake effect” maintains cool, moist microclimate.
leads.rt: If c + c' ≤ 0 ....CTu22 Lake Superior Cliff p. 245

leads.text: Cliff not on immediate shoreline of Lake Superior.
leads.rt: If c + c' > 0 go to d

leads.text: Dry cliff, generally with southeast to west aspect and majority of cliff exposed to direct sunlight. Woody and herbaceous vascular plants, mosses, and algae sparse. Crustose lichens dense.
leads.rt: If d + d' ≤ 0 ....CTn11 Northern Dry Cliff p. 234

leads.text: Dry-mesic to wet cliff, generally with northwest to east aspect and majority of cliff shaded. Woody plants sparse to dense on cliff face. Herbaceous plants have sparse to moderate cover. Mosses, lichens, and algae have moderate to dense cover.
leads.rt: If d + d' > 0 go to e

leads.text: Dry-mesic to mesic cliff with groundwater seepage absent or evident on <1/3 of cliff face. Vascular plants common although largely restricted to crevices and ledges. Mosses, lichens, and algae common; lichens generally have greatest cover. Most commonly on steep slope in North Shore Highlands and Border Lakes subsections; occasionally present in river gorge.
leads.rt: If e + e' < 0 ....CTn32 Northern Mesic Cliff p. 240

leads.text: Wet-mesic to wet cliff with groundwater seepage evident on >1/3 of cliff face. Vascular plants common in crevices, on ledges, and on moss mats on unfractured portions of cliff face. Mosses, lichens, and algae common; mosses and algae usually have highest cover, often forming thick mats. Generally in deep, cool, narrow river gorge (often >50ft [15m] deep and <100ft [30m] wide) in North Shore Highlands Subsection.
leads.rt: If e + e' ≥ 0 ....CTn42 Northern Wet Cliff p. 243

leads.text: Open dry community on exposed bedrock. Shrub and tree cover absent or sparse. Crustose lichens are dominant cover, with foliose species common. Deeper soil surrounding bedrock exposure supports woodland or forest. Small community (<5ac [<2ha]) in opening in woodland or forest on steep slope, ridge top, or summit; also commonly on exposed horizontal or sloping bedrock above cliff.
leads.rt: If a + a' = 0 ....ROn12 Northern Bedrock Outcrop p. 251

leads.text: Shrub-dominated, dry to dry-mesic community on matrix of exposed bedrock and patches of soil. Lichens dominant on exposed bedrock. Woody plants dominant in deeper soil, generally with 25-75% overall cover. Scattered small, open-grown trees common. Evidence of fire often present. Small to medium-sized community (1 to >25ac [0.4 to >10ha]) on ridge top, slope, or summit; occasionally on exposed horizontal or sloping bedrock above cliff.
leads.rt: If a + a' > 0 ....ROn23 Northern Bedrock Shrubland p. 253

leads.text: On sand, gravel, cobble, boulder or bedrock shore along Lake Superior.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 go to b

leads.text: Substrate composed of sand, fine gravel, pebbles, cobbles; most rocks <3ft (1m) long. Usually present in cove, bay, or bay mouth.
leads.rt: If b + b' < 0 ....LKu32 Lake Superior Sand/Gravel/Cobble Shore p. 264

leads.text: Substrate composed of bedrock or large boulders (>3ft [1m] long). Present on tip of point or peninsula, or on long, relatively straight section of shoreline.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≥ 0 ....LKu43 Lake Superior Rocky Shore p. 266

leads.text: On clay, sand, gravel, cobble, boulder, or bedrock shore along inland lake (i.e., lake other than Lake Superior).
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 go to c

leads.text: Substrate ranges from pieces of fractured bedrock and cobbles (<3ft [1m] long), to finer materials such as gravel, sand, clay, or mud. Present on shorelines across Minnesota.
leads.rt: If c + c' < 0 go to d

leads.text: Substrate composed of sand, gravel, or cobbles.
leads.rt: If d + d' < 0 ....LKi32 Inland Lake Sand/Gravel/Cobble Shore p. 259

leads.text: Substrate composed of silt or clay.
leads.rt: If d + d' ≥ 0 ....LKi54 Inland Lake Clay/Mud Shore p. 263

leads.text: Substrate composed of solid rock or large pieces of rock, including solid bedrock outcrops, large pieces of fractured bedrock, or large glacial erratics (>3ft [1m] long). Primarily along lakes on Canadian Shield in Border Lakes Subsection.
leads.rt: If c + c' ≥ 0 ....LKi43 Inland Lake Rocky Shore p. 261

leads.text: Sparsely vegetated river shore, sand bar, or intermittent streambed where primary substrate is sand, gravel, cobbles, boulders, or bedrock.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 go to b

leads.text: River shore, point bar, sand bar, or intermittent streambed with substrate of sand, gravel, or cobbles (<3ft (1m) long).
leads.rt: RVx32 Sand/Gravel/Cobble River Shore p. 270

leads.text: River shore or intermittent streambed with substrate of bedrock or boulders (>3ft [1m] long).
leads.rt: RVx43 Rocky River Shore p. 272

leads.text: Sparsely vegetated river beach, river flat, or steep slumping riverbank with substrate of silt or clay.
leads.rt: If a + a' = 0 ....RVx54 Clay/Mud River Shore p. 274

leads.text: Open peatland in basin or adjacent to lake or stream. Water track features not apparent on aerial photos.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≤ 0 go to b

leads.text: Shrubby peatland dominated by leatherleaf, bog birch, or sweet gale with graminoid layer dominated by broad-leaved sedges and grasses (e.g., bluejoint, lake sedge). Often associated with peatland bordering lake or river shore or in lagg between peatland and upland. Periodically exposed to surface flooding.
leads.rt: If b + b' < -1 ....OPn81 Northern Shrub Shore Fen p. 281

leads.text: Graminoid or shrubby peatland; shrubs if present typically dominated by willows; graminoids dominated by fine-leaved species (e.g., fen wiregrass sedge, creeping sedge [Carex chordorrhiza]). Present in basin or on floating mat adjacent to lake or river. Not exposed to surface flooding.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≥ -1 ....OPn92 Northern Rich Fen (Basin) p. 286

leads.text: Open peatland, typically in large glacial lake plain. Water tracks that follow gradual slope of peatland are usually observable on aerial photos.
leads.rt: If a + a' > 0 ....OPn91 Northern Rich Fen (Water Track) p. 283
WMn82 Northern Wet Meadow/Carr p. 292

leads.text: Emergent marsh in river backwater, bay, or pond; not in setting influenced by water-level fluctuation in Lake Superior.
leads.rt: go to b

leads.text: Dominated by cattails (Typha spp.), usually with >50% cover. Sedges commonly present. Substrate is mineral soil or peat. Often present on floating mat. Associated with sheltered to moderately wave-washed shore.
leads.rt: MRn83 Northern Mixed Cattail Marsh p. 298

leads.text: Dominated by bulrushes or spikerushes (e.g., soft stem bulrush [Scirpus validus], river bulrush [S. fluviatilis], hardstem bulrush [S. acutus], slender bulrush [S. heterochaetus], and Small's spikerush [Eleocharis smallii]). Substrate is mineral soil. Associated with wave-washed shore.
leads.rt: MRn93 Northern Bulrush-Spikerush Marsh p. 299

leads.text: Emergent marsh in river or bay connected to Lake Superior; influenced by fluctuating water levels caused by seiches.
leads.rt: MRu94 Lake Superior Coastal Marsh p. 300

leads.text: Dry conifer woodland occasionally with scattered hardwoods. Canopy dominated by jack pine with red pine [almost never has black spruce or white pine]. On moderately well-drained to excessively well-drained lacustrine sands.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 ....FDn12 Northern Dry-Sand Pine Woodland p. 103

leads.text: Dry-mesic or mesic woodland or forest. Canopy of quaking aspen, black spruce, paper birch, balsam fir, red pine, white pine, or jack pine. On somewhat poorly drained to moderately well-drained lacustrine sands.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 go to b

leads.text: Dry-mesic woodland. Canopy dominated by quaking aspen and black spruce [almost never has jack pine or red maple]. On moderately well to somewhat poorly drained sandy soils.
leads.rt: If b + b' < 0 ....FDn33 Northern Dry-Mesic Mixed Woodland p. 112

leads.text: Poor dry-mesic or mesic woodland or forest. Canopy dominated by jack pine and black spruce; OR canopy composed of quaking aspen, white pine, red pine, paper birch, or balsam fir. On somewhat poorly drained sandy soils.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≥ 0 go to c

leads.text: Poor dry-mesic conifer or occasionally conifer-hardwood woodland. Canopy dominated by jack pine and black spruce, occasionally with quaking aspen [almost never has paper birch, white pine, red pine and red maple]. Most often on very flat sandy lacustrine deposit in the Agassiz Lowlands Subsection.
leads.rt: If c + c' < 0 ....FDn32 Northern Poor Dry-Mesic Mixed Woodland p. 109

leads.text: Mesic conifer-hardwood forest. Canopy dominated by white and red pine, usually with lesser amounts of paper birch and quaking aspen; OR dominated by paper birch and quaking aspen with pine stumps or scattered old pines present [almost never has jack pine or black spruce]. Most often on rolling, coarse-loamy shoreline feature in the Littlefork-Vermilion Uplands Subsection.
leads.rt: If c + c' ≥ 0 ....FDn43 Northern Mesic Mixed Forest p. 115

leads.text: Mesic or wet-mesic hardwood or hardwood-conifer forest. Canopy dominated either by quaking aspen mixed with paper birch and balsam fir OR by basswood, black ash, and sugar maple. Usually on lake plain or moraine.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 go to b

leads.text: Wet-mesic hardwood or hardwood-conifer forest, often with evidence of past conifer dominance. Canopy of quaking aspen, balsam fir, black ash, paper birch [almost never has ironwood]. Usually on very flat terrain (slope <1%) on lake plain or till plain. On moderately well- to poorly drained, coarse-loamy soils, often with some muck on the surface and always with dark, organic-rich surface horizons.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≤ 0 go to c

leads.text: Wet-mesic hardwood or hardwood-conifer forest, usually with evidence of past conifer dominance. Canopy dominated by quaking aspen mixed with balsam fir and paper birch [almost never has basswood]. Most often on fine-sandy lake plain or fine-loamy lake-washed till plain.
leads.rt: If c + c' ≤ 0 ....MHn44 No. Wet-Mesic Boreal Hardwood-Conifer Forest p. 139

leads.text: Wet-mesic hardwood or occasionally hardwood-conifer forest. Canopy dominated by basswood and black ash, sometimes with evidence that scattered conifers were present in past. Most often along river or in drain on fine-loamy alluvium or on lake-washed till plain.
leads.rt: If c + c' > 0 ....MHn46 Northern Wet-Mesic Hardwood Forest p. 144

leads.text: Rich mesic hardwood forest generally lacking conifers, but historically with scattered white pine and white cedar. Canopy dominated by sugar maple and basswood [almost never has quaking aspen, balsam fir, balsam poplar, white spruce, American elm, or bur oak]. Most often on gently sloping site on moraine. On well-drained to moderately well-drained, fine-loamy soils with a thin organic-rich layer over a light-colored leached horizon.
leads.rt: If b + b' > 0 ....MHn47 Northern Rich Mesic Hardwood Forest p. 147

leads.text: Mesic hardwood or rarely hardwood-conifer forest. Canopy of sugar maple, paper birch, quaking aspen, ironwood, bur oak, or basswood [almost never has balsam fir, black ash, white spruce, balsam poplar, or white cedar]. Rare in MOP, documented only on Ponemah Point between Upper and Lower Red Lakes.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 ....MHc37 Central Mesic Hardwood Forest (Western) p. 156

leads.text: Wet riparian hardwood forest. Canopy dominated by black ash and silver maple; often with green ash, basswood, bur oak, or American elm. Most often on rarely or occasionally flooded alluvial or cut terrace along medium or large river. On moderately well-drained to poorly drained silty or, occasionally, sandy soils.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 ....FFn57 Northern Terrace Forest p. 164

leads.text: Very wet riparian hardwood forest. Canopy dominated by silver maple; occasionally with lesser amounts of American elm, green ash, and black ash [bur oak and basswood are absent or have very low abundance]. Most often on annually flooded alluvial plain. On poorly drained sandy soils subject to scouring and deposition from floodwater.
leads.rt: If a + a' ≥ 0 ....FFn67 Northern Floodplain Forest p. 166

leads.text: Wet or very wet conifer, hardwood-conifer, or hardwood forest. Northern Floristic (WFn) Region species present (Table WF-1, p. 172). Canopy dominated by either white cedar or black ash, often with balsam fir and paper birch.
leads.rt: If a + a' < 0 go to b

leads.text: Wet conifer-hardwood forest. Canopy dominated by white cedar mixed with balsam fir and paper birch [almost never has quaking aspen, American elm, balsam poplar, or green ash]. Feathermosses often important in ground layer.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≤ 0 ....WFn53 Northern Wet Cedar Forest p. 177

leads.text: Wet or very wet hardwood or hardwood-conifer forest. Canopy dominated by black ash mixed with quaking aspen, balsam poplar, or American elm [almost never has balsam fir]. Ground layer characterized by sparse cover of dark-green, thin-leaved mosses (Plagiomnium).
leads.rt: If b + b' > 0 go to c

leads.text: Wet hardwood forest, occasionally with scattered conifers. Canopy dominated by black ash [almost never has white cedar or balsam fir].
leads.rt: If c + c' < 0 ....WFn55 Northern Wet Ash Swamp p. 180

leads.text: Very wet hardwood or hardwood-conifer forest. Canopy dominated by black ash [almost never has paper birch, quaking aspen, balsam poplar, American elm or green ash].
leads.rt: If c + c' ≥ 0 ....WFn64 Northern Very Wet Ash Swamp p. 183

leads.text: Wet hardwood forest. Northwestern Floristic (WFw) Region species present (Table WF-3, p.174). Canopy of balsam poplar, quaking aspen, or black ash [almost never has white cedar, balsam fir, or paper birch].

leads.text: Conifer swamp, tree cover >25%; OR shrub swamp dominated by speckled alder, tree cover <25%. Understory species are characteristic of Northern Floristic Region (Table FP-1, p. 193). Present throughout MOP but usually absent from Warroad Till Plain.

leads.text: Shrub swamp dominated by speckled alder, typically with >75% cover. Trees absent or with <25% cover, typically consisting of scattered tamarack, black spruce, paper birch, or black ash.

leads.text: Tree cover >25%, dominated by black spruce, tamarack, or a mixture of the two species.

leads.text: Substrate composed of boulders and rock fragments (talus) eroded from upslope cliff or rock outcrop; generally on steep slope. Very rare (if present at all) in MOP.

leads.text: Substrate composed of vertical or nearly vertical bedrock exposure (cliff), generally greater than 6ft (2m) tall.
leads.rt: If a + a' > 0 go to b

leads.text: Dry cliff, generally with southeast to west aspect; majority of cliff exposed to direct sunlight. Vascular plants, mosses, and algae sparse. Crustose lichens are dominant cover. Trees rare on cliff face. Very rare (if present at all) in MOP.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≤ 0 ....CTn11 Northern Dry Cliff p. 234

leads.text: Dry-mesic to wet cliff, generally with northwest to east aspect; majority of cliff face is shaded (either by tree canopy or because of aspect or setting). Mosses, lichens, and algae have moderate to dense cover. Vascular plants, including woody species, have sparse to moderate cover. Trees usually present on cliff face and often deformed.
leads.rt: If b + b' > 0 go to c

leads.text: Dry-mesic to mesic cliff with groundwater seepage absent or generally limited to less than 1/3 of cliff face. Vascular plants common although largely restricted to crevices and ledges. Mosses, lichens, and algae common, with lichens having greatest cover. Very rare (if present at all) in MOP.
leads.rt: If c + c' < 0 ....CTn32 Northern Mesic Cliff p. 240

leads.text: Wet-mesic to wet cliff with groundwater seepage generally evident on >1/3 of face. Vascular plants common on crevices and ledges as well as in thick moss mats that cover large portions of the cliff. Mosses, lichens, and algae common, with mosses and algae having greatest cover. Very rare (if present at all) in MOP.
leads.rt: If c + c' ≥ 0 ....CTn42 Northern Wet Cliff p. 243

leads.text: Open dry community on exposed bedrock. Shrub and tree cover sparse or absent. Crustose lichens are predominant cover, with foliose species common. Deeper soil surrounding bedrock exposure supports woodland or forest. Small community (<5ac [<2ha]) in opening in woodland or forest on ridge top, slope, or exposed horizontal or sloping bedrock above cliff. Occasional in MOP.
leads.rt: ROn12 Northern Bedrock Outcrop p. 251

leads.text: Shrub-dominated dry to dry-mesic community on matrix of exposed bedrock and deeper soil. Lichens dominant on exposed bedrock. Woody plants dominant on deeper soil, generally with 25-75% cover overall. Scattered small, open-grown trees common. Evidence of fire often present. Small to medium-sized community (1 to >25ac [0.4 to >10ha]) on ridge top, slope, or exposed horizontal or sloping bedrock above cliff. Very rare (if present at all) in MOP.
leads.rt: ROn23 Northern Bedrock Shrubland p. 253

leads.text: Substrate composed of fractured bedrock and cobbles (<3ft [1m] long) or finer materials such as gravel, sand, silt, or clay. Present along lakeshores across Minnesota.

leads.rt: If b + b' < 0 ....LKi32 Inland Lake Sand/Gravel/Cobble Shore p. 259

leads.text: Substrate composed of clay or silt.
leads.rt: If b + b' ≥ 0 ....LKi54 Inland Lake Clay/Mud Shore p. 263

leads.text: Substrate composed of solid rock or large pieces of rock, including bedrock outcrops, large pieces of fractured bedrock, and large glacial erratics (>3ft [1m] long). Uncommon in MOP.
leads.rt: If a + a' = 0 ....LKi43 Inland Lake Rocky Shore p. 261

Present in basin or on floating mat adjacent to lake or river. Not exposed to surface flooding.

leads.text: Open peatland, typically in large glacial lake plain. Water tracks that follow gradual slope of peatland are usually observable on aerial photos.

leads.rt: If c + c' ≤ 0 ....OPn91 Northern Rich Fen (Water Track) p. 283

leads.text: Emergent marsh dominated by cattails (Typha spp.), usually with >50% cover. Sedges commonly present. Substrate is mineral soil or peat. Often present on floating mat. Associated with sheltered to moderately wave-washed shore.
